NIGHT65 builder R round 1 (card Research/2026-10-23-wave65/cards/a5.md, fixed d8972994; DECIDE65 D-3): a5 rebuilt from scratch as THE POUR: the slide-launch. THE TAP WALL (the crucible and its tap block) crosses the middle; its one gap is THE TAP BEAM, a 1.2 m slide-only slot (the tunnel kit; the validator's row 7 proves it); you slide out onto THE APRON among wave 2's husks with THE POUR (lava) 3.5 m ahead and punch them in (a punch while sliding launches). THE GANTRY holds the spitters; THE CRANE RAIL and THE POUR PAD are the fast ways onto it. Every piece has a job and a why.

row.name: 1.5 CRUCIBLE
row.verb36: the slide-launch: slide under THE TAP BEAM, punch the apron's husks into THE POUR (a punch while sliding launches); the parry (a4) answers the spitters' globs (NIGHT65 R, DECIDE65 D-3)
row.pour66_why: NIGHT66 R round 3 (the lead: give THE POUR a body): a launched body flies about 0.43 s (lift 5 m/s) and lands about 6.9 m out, then slides on at the knockback's 16 m/s to about 12.8 m (launch36: 16 m/s for 0.8 s); a grounded body that crosses a pit falls in. So a slide-punch 2-6 m south of THE POUR, facing north, drops the body in the lava; wave 2's two apron bodies are swarmers (a punch launches them: no wind-up, Swarmer.cs; a husk there parries, Parry36.cs:106-114), met at THE TAP BEAM's north mouth by the slide through it
row.waves66_why: NIGHT66 R round 2 (the lead's ask: why the slide punch does not launch, read in the code before re-aiming): a punch on a plain husk inside its 2.2 m melee reach (punch.range is 2.0) that is grounded, free, holds its attack token and is off cooldown is an imminent wind-up, so it resolves as a parry, never a launch (Combat.cs:1397-1401, Parry36.cs:106-114); the husk that walks at you is exactly that body. A swarmer runs its own crouch / pounce / recover states and never sets a wind-up (Swarmer.cs:2-4, :61-95), and Parry36's imminent rule takes only the plain Husk type, so a moving punch always launches it. Round 2b made wave 2's apron pair swarmers: the slide launch fired on one (launch36 1, thrown 12.7 m) but it landed alive in the open, launches came on 4 of 10 skip seeds and set A's deaths went to 2 (r2/r2b). Round 2c / 2d: two of wave 1's six husks are swarmers (a kind level 1 already has, a3): they run ahead of the husks, and a slide-punch launches a swarmer back into the husks behind it or into a wall (the burst: 60 in 3.5 m over a husk's 40 hp; r2d's slide launch from line65[0]: bursts 1, hits 4, kills 4); wave 2 is two husks and two spitters
